transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-21
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Grayline), Ethan Ross (Grayline), Lora Chen (Grayline)

Summary: quick console walkthrough focused on usage analytics and cost per route, with questions about dedicated capacity and security.

00:00 Jared: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jared from redwood, and with me is priya our solutions engineer. today we'll run through the console usage analytics, per-route dashboards and show how cost breaks down at token level, and then leave time for q's.
00:18 Maya: awesome thanks, we just want to see where our spend is coming from and whether dedicated makes sense for our user-facing flows.
00:30 Priya: great, i'll share my screen — okay popped up. so first page is the Usage Overview, this is aggregated across models, regions and routes. you can filter by time range, route tag, model family, quantization profile, etc.
00:55 Ethan: sorry quick q — by route you mean the API route we call from our service, right? not routes like k8s routing?
01:05 Priya: yes, route is our api route identifier — it's what you configure in the routing policy. many customers tag routes by product feature (chat, summarization, recommendations) so costs map to business lines.
01:30 Lora: how granular is attribution? can i see per-team or per-customer spend?
01:40 Priya: you can break down by route, api key, or custom metadata tags. there's also a per-token breakdown that attributes cost to prompt vs generation vs embeddings.
02:02 Priya: switching to Per-Route Dashboards — here we show throughput, p95 latency, token counts, token-cost, and batching efficiency. notice the heatmap on the right — that's per-route token distribution which helps find routes that would benefit from batching or caching.
02:30 Maya: hmm, batching efficiency — is that automatic or we configure it?
02:35 Priya: we have smart batching in the runtime that batches compatible requests; but you can also set route-level targets and batching windows in the deployment config.
02:50 Maya: okay and prefix/KV cache support? we have a lot of repeated prompts for internal search.
02:58 Priya: yes, kv cache and prefix cache show up in the dashboard — you'll see cache hit rates and estimated savings. for repeated prefixes you can save a lot on tokens.
03:20 Ethan: can you show example of how cost changes if we quantize vs run fp16?
03:28 Priya: sure, this is the Cost Breakdown view. on the left is unit cost per token for each model variant — you can compare host fp16, q4_0, q4_1, and our recommended quantization profile per workload.
03:45 Priya: note these are estimates derived from your historical sequence length distribution; the console projects monthly spend under different model/quantization configs.
04:08 Maya: these numbers look promising, but our main ask is predictable spend. we can't have surprises mid-quarter.
04:17 Jared: totally — that's where Dedicated comes in. with dedicated pools you commit capacity and we guarantee throughput SLA. we can show committed burst options for traffic spikes.
04:30 Lora: and on procurement — do you offer monthly vs annual for dedicated? we usually prefer annual with budget certs.
04:40 Jared: yes both. we'll include committed monthly and annual pricing in the proposal.
04:48 Ethan: security wise we need VPC/private deployment for PCI-regulated flows, and encryption keys managed in our KMS.
04:55 Priya: we support Private deployments and integrations with customer KMS/HSM. the console will still show usage but logs are written to your audit bucket; you can opt into a customer-managed control plane for on-prem.
05:10 Maya: do you have SOC 2 and ISO attestation?
05:14 Jared: yes SOC 2 Type II, and we can share the report under nda — we'll attach the security whitepaper.
05:22 Priya: quick demo — clicking into a route, here's the timeline of requests, tokens/req, average latency, and an estimated cost-per-1000-requests. you can also overlay commits and capacity reservations so you see expected vs actual spend.
06:05 Ethan: the latency numbers seem to vary a lot — is that because of large sequence lengths?
06:12 Priya: exactly, seq length distribution drives latency. the console correlates latency spikes with model variant, batch size and caching; you can drill into problematic samples and see the raw traces.
06:35 Maya: can you export this data for our internal finance team? csv or bigquery?
06:40 Priya: yes export to csv and export streams to BigQuery/S3. many finance teams use the token-level billing export to map costs into their cost center chart of accounts.
07:00 Jared: another feature — cost anomalies and alerting. you can set alerts on spend rate or per-route token increase; we also have quality regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets so you don't regress when swapping quantization.
07:30 Lora: good, procurement will want the alerting in writing for SLAs.
07:35 Jared: we'll include the alerting policy language in the offer.
07:40 Priya: switching to the Demo Kit — this is a sample benchmark sheet we run with customers for pilot: traffic profile, representative prompts, p50/p95 latency, and token-per-call distribution.
08:05 Ethan: for the pilot, can we use our eval dataset? we have production traffic anonymized.
08:12 Priya: absolutely, use your traffic and we'll set up a dedicated benchmark run against a hosted and a dedicated variant. helps quantify cost delta and latency tradeoffs.
08:30 Maya: ok what's a typical delta between hosted and dedicated on unit cost?
08:36 Jared: it depends on utilization. if you're consistently high QPS, dedicated tends to lower unit cost because of sustained utilization and reserved pricing. hosted is better if traffic is bursty and you want low operational overhead.
08:56 Priya: also consider caching and batching — sometimes right batching config closes most of the gap without full dedicated commit.
09:10 Ethan: any caveats on model compatibility with dedicated? like certain optimized kernels or fp16 only?
09:18 Priya: dedicated supports the same model catalog. the runtime will pick kernels and quantized variants based on the hardware. occasionally niche models need tuning but we surface kernel choices in the console.
09:40 Maya: are there per-route rate limits we can enforce at the console? we want graceful degradation for lower-tier customers.
09:48 Priya: yes rate limiting and route-level fallback policies are available. you can do canary rollouts and automatic fallback to lighter model variants when latency SLOs are at risk.
10:10 Lora: what about audit logs for compliance? we need immutable logs for a year.
10:18 Jared: audit logs are exportable to your S3 or SIEM — retention policies configurable per account.
10:30 Maya: okay let's look at the cost projection scenario — Priya can you switch to the projections widget?
10:36 Priya: sure — here's projected monthly spend by route based on current traffic. i can toggle model variant to show how q4_0 reduces costs but may increase small regressions.
11:05 Maya: what's the best way to show cost per customer for chargeback?
11:10 Priya: use API key tagging per customer and the per-key export; also the per-route dashboard supports synthesis to a chargeback csv.
11:30 Ethan: can the console show token delta for generated tokens vs prompt tokens? we need to know which flows cause generation spikes.
11:38 Priya: yes it's displayed as prompt vs generation vs embedding tokens. for embeddings it's per-embedding unit.
12:00 Maya: a question on billing granularity — do you round at 1 token increments or something like 8?
12:08 Priya: tokens are metered at token-level; we show both billed tokens and raw token counts. sometimes transcription differences cause slight mismatch but billing aligns to metered tokens.
12:30 Jared: moving on — an example customer case: Nova-Commerce reduced unit costs 27% by combining prefix cache and q4_1 on non-critical routes and moving high-volume low-latency flows to dedicated.
13:00 Maya: nice, can you share that case study?
13:05 Jared: yes i'll add it to the follow-up.
13:12 Priya: now demoing the route detail — here you can pin important metrics, add notes, and open a sample trace. see the trace viewer, it's not perfect transcription, occasional words are off but you get the sequence length and KV hits.
13:40 Ethan: i see an example of high p99 — what's the root cause?
13:45 Priya: if you click the trace it shows a long generation and a cache miss; that route had many long prompts causing large kv cache pressure.
14:05 Maya: any way to auto-suggest optimizations?
14:10 Priya: yes Optimize recommendations — it suggests batching windows, quantization profiles, and routes that could benefit from caching. those are surfaced in the console under "Optimize".
14:30 Lora: procurement question — for dedicated do you provide a SOC2 addendum and vendor attestations?
14:38 Jared: yes we provide SOC2 report and can include security addendum in enterprise contracts.
14:45 Ethan: latency SLOs — are these contractual? p95 < 350ms for the flows we care about?
14:53 Jared: for dedicated we can agree on p95 SLAs but need to define sequence length buckets. we'll map your traffic to buckets as part of the pilot.
15:20 Priya: switching to the billing export — here's the token-level billing CSV columns: timestamp, route_id, api_key, model_variant, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, billed_tokens, cost_usd. you can import this to your finance system.
15:50 Maya: perfect. does the console show savings per-route if we enable prefix cache?
15:56 Priya: yes it shows estimated monthly savings and ROI for cache vs implementation effort. usually we show a delta chart.
16:15 Ethan: about fallback policies — can i route to cheaper model variant when p95 > threshold automatically?
16:22 Priya: yes, route policies can be configured to fallback based on latency, error rate, or cost budgets.
16:40 Maya: are there native dashboards for app metrics or do we need to integrate our observability stack?
16:45 Priya: you can export traces to Datadog/NewRelic and we have built-in dashboards; many teams integrate with their observability stack for end-to-end correlation.
17:05 Lora: procurement needs a clear line item for dedicated pool sizing — do you provide sizing guidance?
17:12 Jared: SEs do sizing once we see traffic; for now we'll include a recommended commit range and burst capacity. Priya can put numbers in the proposal.
17:30 Priya: jumping back to Optimize tab — recommendations are ranked by estimated $ savings and impact to latency/quality. you can accept or reject suggestions and apply them to one route or to all routes with similar profile.
18:00 Maya: how do you validate quality changes after quantization? we can't regress user experience.
18:07 Priya: we have eval harness and quality monitoring that runs prompt sets and alerts on regressions; the console shows example diffs and rollback buttons.
18:30 Ethan: great, curious about integration effort — how long until pilot?
18:36 Jared: typically 2-3 weeks to run pilot: data prep + run benchmarks + analyze results.
18:45 Maya: okay that's reasonable. Lora will own procurement timeline.
18:52 Lora: procurement needs vendor legal and pricing by next tuesday.
19:00 Jared: we'll aim for that.
19:10 Priya: quick note — we also surface per-route cost-per-conversation for chat flows so product teams can understand unit economics.
19:28 Maya: can you show how that per-conversation calc works?
19:32 Priya: it's tokens-per-convo * cost-per-token; we let you define conversation boundaries in the console so it aligns to your UX metrics.
19:50 Ethan: any gotchas with embeddings billing? we have large-scale similarity indexing.
19:57 Priya: embeddings are billed per-embedding unit; console shows cost per-embedding and suggests batching and truncation strategies.
20:20 Maya: what about cold-start latencies on dedicated pools?
20:27 Priya: cold start is minimal on dedicated; hosted cold starts can be more variable. we also offer warmers and pre-warming policies.
20:45 Lora: are there cross-account role options? we need RBAC so product and finance teams can see different views.
20:52 Priya: yes RBAC and SSO/SAML are built-in, console roles include viewer, analyst, ops, admin.
21:10 Jared: let's do a quick recap and next steps.
21:16 Jared: recap: we showed usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown, optimize recommendations, and covered dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, security and export options.
21:30 Jared: agreed next steps: Jared to send pricing and committed capacity options; Priya to prepare benchmark plan and screenshots; Maya to share traffic profile.
21:50 Maya: sounds good. one last tiny question — will the console keep raw traces for 90 days by default?
21:58 Priya: default is 30 days for traces, audit logs configurable up to 365 days or more depending on plan.
22:12 Lora: okay thank you.
22:15 Jared: thanks all, we'll follow up with the deck and security docs.
22:20 Meeting end.

Note: transcript contains occasional imperfect transcription (names, product tokens) and filler words as typical of fireflies exports.
